(u4, else) -> u4
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved, u1) -> 0.1
(u0, key_lost, u0) -> -0.2
(u1, has_door_key, u2) -> 0.1
(u2, door_open & has_door_key, u3) -> 1.0
(u2, key_lost, u1) -> -0.2
(u3, target_picked_up, u4) -> -2.0
feedback: Accepted with minor notes. The RM is format-compliant: all required headers present, FINAL_STATES (u3) is nonempty, declared in STATES, and accepting for the task (door opened after key-holding, box never picked up). Semantic fidelity is good: the hard 'never pick up the box' constraint is encoded as (u3, target_picked_up) -> u4 with -2.0 into a rewardless dead sink — correct, since target_picked_up can only fire when the door is open, i.e., in u3; the soft 'try not to drop the key while the door is still closed' preference is penalized per key_lost occurrence (-0.2) in u0 and u2, the only pre-goal states where the event can fire (key_lost is impossible in u1 because any prior-step has_door_key would have moved the machine to u2); and 'open it later' is honored by the explicit regression (u2, key_lost) -> u1 that lets the agent re-acquire the key and still collect the +1.0. Reachability holds: u3 is reachable via a valid solution and no unintended dead ends exist. Reward safety holds: progress rewards (+0.1, +0.1, +1.0) are dense and bounded; the only re-earnable positive (+0.1 via u1->u2) is dominated by the -0.2 drop cost, and u3 is a one-way absorbing goal state, so the +1.0 cannot be farmed — importantly, this is why u3 must NOT regress on door-closing or key_lost (any u3->u1/u2 regression would let open/close/drop/re-pick cycles re-earn +1.0). Per-state else self-loops cover all irrelevant or unfireable propositions. Two minor, non-blocking notes: (1) in the corner where the agent deliberately toggles the open door shut and then drops the key, key_lost fires in u3 and is absorbed by else without the -0.2 penalty; a rewardless-state-safe fix would be a (u3, key_lost) self-loop at -0.2 rather than a regression, but the omission only forgoes a penalty in a pathological behavior and creates no reward inflation. (2) The guard 'door_open & has_door_key' is redundant (the door can only first open while the key is held) but harmless and defensively correct. The choice to leave has_door_key unrewarded in u0 is sound: the key-first order forces a key drop (penalized), and the eventual chain u1->u2->u3 still delivers the full shaping, matching the ball-first canonical trace.

feedback: All five environment-declared propositions are implemented and no extra functions are present. `has_door_key`, `door_open`, and `target_picked_up` match the reference expressions exactly (carrying check with color-matched door scan; `is_open` on doors; mission-templated box check), all reading only current state, correctly persistent. `key_lost` is a correct event: it reads the read-only `env.episode_memory['previous_valuation']` snapshot, requires previous `has_door_key` true, current has_door_key false, and current door_open false, so it holds for exactly one step after the drop with no latching; the leading `bool(...)` guard is redundant (the snapshot is a non-empty complete valuation, and it is all-false at step 0 so the event is still false then) but harmless and purely read-only. `blocker_moved` deviates structurally from the reference (it scans for any door with `x > 0` whose left/front cell `(x-1, y)` holds a ball, rather than locating the unique door first), but since the environment guarantees exactly one door in the shared wall with the start room on the left and the ball at `(dx-1, dy)`, this is semantically equivalent: true when that cell holds no ball (a carried ball is off-grid, so it counts as moved), false again if the ball is dropped back there, and the `x > 0` guard short-circuits safely before indexing `x-1`. No imports, no actions, no side effects, no mutation of env or episode memory; short-circuit guards prevent attribute access on None; all attribute uses (`type`, `color`, `is_open`, `carrying`, `mission`, `width`, `height`, `grid.get`) are within the documented API; syntax is valid. The never-coholden constraints (`key_lost` vs `has_door_key`/`door_open`) are enforced directly by the event definition.
